assumptions.statement: Exactly ONE money gate is sufficient to prevent every unsafe spend across the whole system.
assumptions.evidence_for: F1/F2/F1.b closed (commits 05927dad/299b1247/f4d67f34); chronica-policy evaluate_gate is the shared deterministic verdict function used by tracked money paths; snapshot shows 0 moves_money∧¬requires_approval. Issue #3183 corrected the stronger topology claim: production enforcement has multiple direct callers, and arch:verify possible_bypass_files=0 is literal-smoke evidence, not callgraph or single-funnel proof.
assumptions.evidence_against: F3 is a SECOND ungated mint in chronica-internet-hand (present code, un-wired) — proof the one-gate property is a discipline, not a structural guarantee; three prior holes (F1/F2/F1.b) all slipped past review once; any new crate can add a money sink that forgets the gate.

assumptions.statement: A Rust-only backend (no production Python) is the correct call for a money-handling holding OS.
assumptions.evidence_for: Type/memory safety + deterministic financial math; single auditable money path; 1189 caps verified natively with real tests.
assumptions.evidence_against: ~39% verified after ~a year (1189/3013) — porting cost is enormous and still mostly ahead; ML/analytics donor logic is awkward to port; no production-load validation yet.

assumptions.statement: The survivable-side-table pattern (caps.db gitignored + committed JSON re-applied by reconcile-*) is a sound durable-state design.
assumptions.evidence_for: Survives the 937MB caps.db wipe on every rebuild; meta drift now gated by reconcile-meta --check; 5 dim tables already ride it.
assumptions.evidence_against: A forgotten reconcile step silently drops data with no error; meta already rotted 59× once before the --check gate existed; architecture.db has NO side-table (fully rederived), so its control-links/invariants live only in a generator — a divergent durability story.

assumptions.statement: Deny-by-default ScopePath tenancy (DB-derived account_id + require_company_scope) fully isolates tenants.
assumptions.evidence_for: The LIVE-DB route test dev_token_for_another_account_cannot_read_a_company (chronica-api/tests/dev_auth_route.rs) proves a REAL signed bearer minted for account B gets 403 on account A's company — DB-authoritative tenancy, real runtime; assert_company_access_scoped guards the money-actions + approvals routes too (approvals.rs:234); DB account_id re-derived per company route; deployed-binary smoke 7d706d95; ScopePath::contains reused not forked.
assumptions.evidence_against: The FULLY/complete claim is unproven across ALL routes — the guard is per-route convention (assert_company_access_scoped / require_company_scope), not a compile-time guarantee, so a new route that forgets it would leak; and the live-authed UI click-through end-to-end (real human session, bearer-attach, zero leak across the whole surface) is still unproven.

assumptions.statement: An event backbone + read-model consumers (CQRS) is necessary foundation the system currently lacks.
assumptions.evidence_for: Ranked #1 by strategy-graph leverage (unlocks 7 downstream); would decouple write path from feed/OLAP/agent-memory read models.
assumptions.evidence_against: NOTHING built today actually requires it — synchronous inline read-model projection already gives read-after-write (commit e24007d3); it may be premature architecture whose leverage is graph-asserted, not demand-proven. The graph could be over-rewarding it.

assumptions.statement: ClickHouse is the right OLAP store for live KPIs/analytics.
assumptions.evidence_for: PostHog/ClickHouse donor absorbed; columnar store fits BusinessEvent aggregation.
assumptions.evidence_against: Not wired; Postgres very likely suffices at current (zero-prod-traffic) scale; a second datastore is standing operational debt until there is real query volume to justify it.

assumptions.statement: Calibration-earned trust tiers (track-record → authority ceiling) are the right model for agent autonomy.
assumptions.evidence_for: chronica-strategy calibration (PlayerCalibration) built; cold-start = lowest trust is conservative-by-default.
assumptions.evidence_against: No live agents have earned any trust yet — the calibration math is untested against real outcomes; a mis-tuned tier could over-grant autonomy; trust tiers never touch money regardless, so blast radius is bounded.

assumptions.statement: The 74 donor repos are enough capability coverage for a complete Company OS.
assumptions.evidence_against: 'Enough' is unmeasured; donor utilization shows many barely mined (playwright 0% built; node_exporter/loki/kube-state-metrics 0% scouted); 16 live competitive-market GAPS suggest real coverage holes no donor fills.

assumptions.statement: An X/Twitter-style operational feed is the right primary product surface for operators.
assumptions.evidence_for: User rejected the control-room dashboard 3× and chose feed-first; 150/150 feed vitest + live X-styled preview.
assumptions.evidence_against: Never tested with a real operator running real companies; 50+ concurrent agents in a single feed is unproven UX; business users may still want dashboards alongside the feed.

assumptions.statement: Porting donor capabilities natively into Rust beats integrating them as external services.
assumptions.evidence_for: One monolith → one money gate, one audit chain, one ERP truth; no runtime-state confusion between layers.
assumptions.evidence_against: Porting cost is enormous; external SELLING surfaces are explicitly NOT ported (connector layer) — the internal-absorb / external-connect line is a judgment call that could move and partly invalidate the bet.

assumptions.statement: Board-only money approval can scale to the decision frequency a running holding company needs.
assumptions.evidence_for: Auto-allow handles trivial (<~$5) spend; idempotent single-use approvals make the path safe under retry/concurrency.
assumptions.evidence_against: Board is a structural bottleneck at high frequency; no load test exists; if real operations need thousands of money decisions/day the human-in-loop gate may not keep up — a throughput risk, not a safety risk.

assumptions.statement: Forcing every serious action to link ERP/finance state (or declare no_erp_impact) is tractable and complete.
assumptions.evidence_for: ERP is system-of-record; binding objects + 10 verify rules defined; commerce/integrations map effects back to ERP.
assumptions.evidence_against: Enforcement is by convention + verify rules, not a hard compile-time gate — an action can skip the linkage and only a reviewer catches it; 'completeness' of the ERP schema for all business events is asserted, not proven.

assumptions.statement: A Temporal-style durable workflow runtime is the right backbone for long-running business loops.
assumptions.evidence_for: 54% built (134/247); durable_state + history_management ported; unlocks billing/SLA/lifecycle automation downstream.
assumptions.evidence_against: Crash-safety under real load is unproven; durable-execution correctness is notoriously subtle; building the wrong durability model is expensive to unwind once business loops depend on it.

assumptions.statement: The docs + capabilities.db two-surface system stays synchronized in practice.
assumptions.evidence_for: docs:gen/sync/verify round-trip; docs:verify gates drift in CI; reconcile-meta --check guards meta counts.
assumptions.evidence_against: Sync holds only if docs:gen/verify are actually run every time — meta silently rotted 59× before the --check gate; hand-written prose docs (xx30-69) have no generator and drift until a manual re-grounding pass.

assumptions.statement: A capability marked 'verified' is actually correct, not just compiling with a passing test.
assumptions.underpins: every progress/end-state percentage the tracker reports
assumptions.evidence_for: record-verified refuses a row whose test symbol is absent; verify-impl-evidence green 1189/1189; money caps require a financial_control_test.
assumptions.evidence_against: MEASURED 2026-06-20: 1064/1189 verified caps (90%) rest on a co-located (src/) inline unit test; only 125 (10%) have an integration/route test (tests/) — so most 'verified' caps lack route/live-DB proof. The live-DB route suite is env-blocked locally; 'green ≠ correct' — business-logic bugs (F1/F2) passed all tests once; the headline rests partly on docs:sync stamps, not independent re-proof.
